Fatty acids must be activated in the cytosol by binding to coenzyme A (forming acyl-CoA) before transport into mitochondria, but acyl-CoA cannot directly cross the inner mitochondrial membrane.  
Instead, the acyl group is transferred from CoA to carnitine by carnitine palmitoyltransferase I (CPT I) in the outer mitochondrial membrane.  
The resulting acyl-carnitine is shuttled across the inner membrane via the carnitine-acylcarnitine translocase.  
Once inside, carnitine palmitoyltransferase II (CPT II) transfers the acyl group back to CoA, freeing carnitine to return to the cytosol.  
Thus, during the actual transport step across the mitochondrial membrane, fatty acids are bound to carnitine.
